random.title: 01 · Long dice branches
random.question: How does repeated sampling change the occupancy of long branches?

random.title: 02 · Biased coin walk
random.question: Compare a drifted coin walk with an independent zero-mean reference.

random.title: 03 · Persistent paths
random.question: What changes when the next increment tends to repeat the last?

random.title: 04 · Gaussian increments
random.question: Explore the spread of independent normal-increment paths.

random.title: 05 · Uniform increments
random.question: Compare bounded increments with Gaussian paths using the same standard deviation.

random.title: 06 · Laplace tails
random.question: Keep mean 0 and standard deviation 1, but increase the probability of large increments.

random.title: 07 · Triangular increments
random.question: A symmetric triangular law has bounded support and more weight near the mean.

random.title: 08 · Brownian drift
random.question: Compare positive drift with zero drift at the same diffusion coefficient.

random.title: 09 · Critical branching
random.question: Critical Poisson offspring has mean one; individual populations may still become extinct.

random.title: 10 · Subcritical offspring
random.question: Explore extinction with binomial offspring mean 0.8.

random.title: 11 · Immigration & turnover
random.question: Immigration can restore a population after it reaches zero.

random.title: 12 · Your offspring law
random.question: Modify an explicit offspring probability table; mean offspring here is one.

random.title: 13 · Sierpiński arrivals
random.question: Watch contractions accumulate a triangle; inspect the finite sample rather than assuming a dimension estimate.

random.title: 14 · Resource-limited colony
random.question: Compare growth with barriers and resources to the same rules without the environment.

random.title: 15 · Exponential waiting increments
random.question: Sum positive waiting-time samples and inspect their skewed increment distribution.

random.title: 16 · Gamma accumulation
random.question: Explore shape 3, scale 0.5: positive increments have mean 1.5 and variance 0.75.

random.title: 17 · Lognormal bursts
random.question: Rare large positive increments dominate some paths; log(X) is Gaussian.

random.title: 18 · Beta bounded increments
random.question: Inspect a right-skewed distribution whose increments are constrained to [0,1].

random.title: 19 · Weibull shape exploration
random.question: A shape below one concentrates many increments near zero while retaining a long right tail.

random.title: 20 · Student t heavy tails
random.question: With ν=3, the variance exists but extremes are more frequent than under a Gaussian law.

random.title: 21 · Cauchy limit of Student t
random.question: With ν=1, population mean and variance do not exist. A finite sample mean is not a stable population summary.

random.title: 22 · Geometric offspring
random.question: Counts failures before success: p=0.55 makes this branching process subcritical.

plants.title: 01 · Shared environment
plants.question: Compare three pathway presets under identical forcing. Traits remain illustrative, not cultivar fits.

plants.title: 02 · Sowing to grain filling
plants.question: Follow thermal-time leaf emergence and reproductive carbon allocation over 150 days.

plants.title: 03 · Drought without rescue
plants.question: Track soil depletion, carbon assimilation and organ construction without irrigation.

plants.title: 04 · Threshold irrigation
plants.question: Investigate whether replenishment preserves carbon and reproductive tissue.

plants.title: 05 · Nitrogen shortage
plants.question: Compare the resulting plant with the shared-environment record. Nitrogen supply is reduced.

plants.title: 06 · Fertilizer pulses
plants.question: Track soil nitrogen replenishment and uptake; doses are model inputs, not agronomic recommendations.

plants.title: 07 · C4 cooling hypothesis
plants.question: Test conditional C4 cooling with a cooler soil sink. Use the paired cooling panels.

plants.title: 08 · Warm soil sink
plants.question: Repeat the cooling hypothesis with warmer soil: the heat sink is less effective.

plants.title: 09 · Seasonal temperate profile
plants.question: Use Düsseldorf latitude and calendar-driven light with an illustrative linked climate.

plants.title: 10 · Sahel profile
plants.question: Use Niamey latitude, seasonality and linked illustrative weather; this is not a measured field site.

plants.title: 11 · CAM water economy
plants.question: Compare agave-like and other pathway presets under low water, over full day/night cycles.

plants.title: 12 · Alternative architectures
plants.question: Inspect wheat, sorghum and prickly pear using the same organ-state renderer.

plants.title: 13 · Shaded canopy
plants.question: How does lower light change leaf production, reserves and harvest tissue?

plants.title: 14 · Elevated carbon dioxide
plants.question: Compare C3, C4 and CAM productivity at 700 ppm with the shared-environment example.

plants.title: 15 · Scheduled irrigation
plants.question: Apply water on a fixed schedule and inspect soil depletion between irrigation events.

plants.title: 16 · Wind and evaporative demand
plants.question: Increase wind at fixed radiation and humidity; inspect leaf energy balance and soil water use.

plants.title: 17 · Tropical seasonal growth
plants.question: Use the Yaoundé calendar and linked illustrative weather to follow production over a growing season.

plants.title: 18 · Wheat and sorghum development
plants.question: Follow thermal-time leaf appearance and reproductive allocation with wheat, sorghum and prickly pear architectures.

tcells.title: 01 · Activation & division
tcells.question: Compare the stochastic ensemble with reference moments.

tcells.title: 02 · Activation bottleneck
tcells.question: Delay first activation while retaining subsequent proliferation rates.

tcells.title: 03 · Division without death
tcells.question: Follow generation-limited proliferation and the absorbing final generation.

tcells.title: 04 · Activation without division
tcells.question: Separate activation from production of daughter cells.

tcells.title: 05 · Birth–death model
tcells.question: Compare direct stochastic division/death with the mean ODE.

tcells.title: 06 · Bellman–Harris / Erlang
tcells.question: Lifetimes depend on age; fate is selected before the conditional lifetime is drawn.

tcells.title: 07 · Broad lifetime variation
tcells.question: Use lognormal conditional lifetimes with coefficient of variation 0.8.

tcells.title: 08 · Synchronized cohorts
tcells.question: Use deterministic lifetimes to reveal division waves.

tcells.title: 09 · Cyton competition
tcells.question: Independent division and death clocks compete; division competence is not survival probability.

tcells.title: 10 · Multitype generations
tcells.question: Discrete generation cycles are not chronological hours.

tcells.title: 11 · Memoryless lifetimes
tcells.question: An exponential lifetime provides a memoryless reference for age-dependent models.

tcells.title: 12 · Narrow age-dependent cohorts
tcells.question: Compare Erlang shape 8 with shape 3 at unchanged mean lifetimes; watch division synchrony.

tcells.title: 13 · Delayed first division
tcells.question: Lengthen the first division clock while keeping later divisions fast.

tcells.title: 14 · Shorter-lived cells
tcells.question: Shorten the conditional death lifetime; fate probabilities remain unchanged.

tcells.title: 15 · Cyton survival competition
tcells.question: Give the death clock a longer mean and inspect how many divisions win the competing-clock race.

tcells.title: 16 · Cyton fixed clocks
tcells.question: Use fixed division and death clocks to make event order and generation waves visible.

tcells.title: 17 · A single founder
tcells.question: Follow one complete founder lineage and compare its stochastic outcome with the ensemble.

tcells.title: 18 · Longer multitype lineage
tcells.question: Allow eight generations and inspect the final-generation boundary in discrete cycles.

lipids.title: 01 · Thesis parameter preset
lipids.question: Inspect chain elongation, product release and CoA inhibition.

lipids.title: 02 · Remove CoA inhibition
lipids.question: Compare both inhibition states from the same starting substrate pools.

lipids.title: 03 · Limited reducing power
lipids.question: Reduce NADPH to constrain reductive chain elongation.

lipids.title: 04 · Malonyl limitation
lipids.question: Reduce the two-carbon donor pool and inspect product concentrations.

lipids.title: 05 · Greater enzyme capacity
lipids.question: Double FAS at unchanged substrates; inspect substrate exhaustion and product formation.

lipids.title: 06 · Earlier C14 release
lipids.question: Increase C14 release and inspect the product spectrum.

lipids.title: 07 · Enhanced C18 elongation
lipids.question: Increase the final elongation rate; this is a hypothetical parameter intervention.

lipids.title: 08 · CoA-rich start
lipids.question: Explore enzyme sequestration by an initial free CoA pool.

lipids.title: 09 · Four metabolic pools
lipids.question: Compare distinct initial conditions under the same four-pool rate laws.

lipids.title: 10 · Increased lipid influx
lipids.question: Change fatty-acid influx and follow redistribution among pools.

lipids.title: 11 · Storage capacity
lipids.question: Increase the storage flux capacity. No bistability claim is attached to these equations.

lipids.title: 12 · Acetyl-CoA limitation
lipids.question: Reduce the initiation substrate; compare initiation, enzyme occupancy and total released products.

lipids.title: 13 · Slow initiation
lipids.question: Reduce the initiation rate and inspect the delay before chains accumulate.

lipids.title: 14 · C16 release preference
lipids.question: Increase release from EC16 and inspect C16:0 concentration and product fraction together.

lipids.title: 15 · Faster CoA dissociation
lipids.question: Increase inhibitor dissociation while keeping binding unchanged.

lipids.title: 16 · Reduced FAS abundance
lipids.question: Lower enzyme concentration tenfold at unchanged substrates; compare production rate and final yield.

lipids.title: 17 · Faster triglyceride mobilization
lipids.question: Increase V5 and follow storage-pool depletion and fatty-acid recovery.

lipids.title: 18 · Feedback removal
lipids.question: Remove both feedback inhibition terms and examine the new transient and calculated equilibrium.

evolution.title: 01 · Kimura + CMA-ES
evolution.question: Compare stochastic origin–fixation paths with scalar numerical search.

evolution.title: 02 · Pareto search
evolution.question: Inspect carbon–water trade-offs without treating optimizer steps as generations.

evolution.title: 03 · Epsilon constraints
evolution.question: Maximize carbon under explicit water and heat caps.

evolution.title: 04 · Neutral reference
evolution.question: Set the performance-to-selection scale to zero; fixation is neutral.

evolution.title: 05 · Warm, humid location
evolution.question: Build an illustrative Yaoundé forcing cycle and examine water–carbon trade-offs. Dry sites may fail the hydraulic or heat constraints.

evolution.title: 06 · Replicate uncertainty
evolution.question: Compare ten seeded origin–fixation trajectories from the same initial condition.

evolution.title: 07 · Smaller effective population
evolution.question: Compare neutral fixation and waiting times at Ne = 20; census mutation supply is held constant.

evolution.title: 08 · Larger effective population
evolution.question: Compare neutral substitution waiting times at Ne = 400; no selection is imposed.

evolution.title: 09 · Reduced mutation supply
evolution.question: Reduce mutation rate tenfold; compare biological waiting times rather than optimizer iterations.

evolution.title: 10 · Stronger performance selection
evolution.question: Increase the performance-to-selection scale and inspect fixation biases. This is a modeling assumption.

evolution.title: 11 · Carbon-centered objective
evolution.question: Set water and heat penalties to zero while retaining physiological feasibility constraints.

evolution.title: 12 · Water-aware productivity
evolution.question: Increase the water-use penalty while retaining the reward for carbon assimilation.

evolution.title: 13 · Thermal-risk penalty
evolution.question: Increase the heat penalty; evaluate carbon and heat together when judging the endpoint.

evolution.title: 14 · C4-like starting resident
evolution.question: Start near a C4 allocation and test path dependence under the same forcing.

evolution.title: 15 · Intermediate starting resident
evolution.question: Start with an intermediate allocation. The model does not implement a complete C2 mechanism.

evolution.title: 16 · Stricter water constraint
evolution.question: Compare epsilon-constrained feasible candidates under a reduced water cap; an empty set is a valid result.

evolution.title: 17 · Finer allocation grid
evolution.question: Increase allocation resolution to distinguish a coarse-grid endpoint from a stable search result.

evolution.title: 18 · Longer Pareto search
evolution.question: Increase NSGA-II iterations to inspect convergence of the approximate carbon–water–heat front.

evolution.title: 19 · Temperate growing season
evolution.question: How does selection across a 90-day season differ from a single repeated day? Compare stress timing while holding the evolutionary horizon fixed.

evolution.title: 20 · Tropical dry-season pressure
evolution.question: How does selection across a 120-day season differ from a single repeated day? Compare stress timing while holding the evolutionary horizon fixed.

evolution.title: 21 · Highland seasonal comparison
evolution.question: How does selection across a 90-day season differ from a single repeated day? Compare stress timing while holding the evolutionary horizon fixed.

leaf.title: 01 · C3-like allocation
leaf.question: Compare carbon uptake and water loss when Rubisco is allocated to the mesophyll.

leaf.title: 02 · C4-like allocation
leaf.question: Inspect the energy cost of the carbon-concentration mechanism.

leaf.title: 03 · Intermediate allocation
leaf.question: A biochemical allocation experiment; this is not a complete C2 intermediate.

leaf.title: 04 · Humid air
leaf.question: Change relative humidity while holding temperature and stomata fixed.

leaf.title: 05 · Dry air
leaf.question: Inspect leaf-to-air vapor demand under drier air.

leaf.title: 06 · Dry soil
leaf.question: Compare hydraulic supply with evaporative demand.

leaf.title: 07 · Reduced stomatal opening
leaf.question: Compare carbon gain, transpiration and leaf temperature at lower conductance.

leaf.title: 08 · Low irradiance
leaf.question: Test assimilation under a constrained photochemical energy supply.

leaf.title: 09 · Warm leaf environment
leaf.question: Inspect the effect of a 35 °C air boundary on solved leaf temperatures.

leaf.title: 10 · Cool soil boundary
leaf.question: Prescribe a cooler root zone and inspect the thermal balance.

leaf.title: 11 · Elevated CO2 boundary
leaf.question: Inspect the solved carbon-concentration mechanism at 700 ppm atmospheric CO2.

leaf.title: 12 · C3 elevated CO2
leaf.question: Compare C3 and C4 responses to the same elevated CO2 boundary.

leaf.title: 13 · Higher irradiance
leaf.question: Increase irradiance and inspect ATP supply, assimilation and solved temperatures.

leaf.title: 14 · Reduced biochemical capacity
leaf.question: Reduce total Rubisco capacity and compare carbon uptake with water use.

leaf.title: 15 · Lower cyclic electron capacity
leaf.question: Reduce the cyclic-electron-flow setting; inspect ATP supply and carbon limitation.

leaf.title: 16 · Greater cyclic electron capacity
leaf.question: Increase the cyclic-electron-flow setting and inspect the energy budget.

leaf.title: 17 · Warm root-zone boundary
leaf.question: Prescribe a warmer soil boundary and compare solved leaf energy balance with the cool-soil case.

leaf.title: 18 · C4 cooling hypothesis
leaf.question: Enable the conditional C4-only controller under a hot, humid boundary with cooler prescribed soil.
